description: A team project that takes one computing idea from proposal to defended demonstration, whatever the domain. In the lab students frame a problem, plan and track the work, build and test a deliverable, evaluate it honestly and present it to a mock panel.
modelledOn: Sommerville, Software Engineering (project management and process chapters)
Booth, Colomb and Williams, The Craft of Research
PMBOK Guide, Project Management Institute (planning and risk processes)
Brooke, SUS: A quick and dirty usability scale (usability evaluation practice)
outcomes: Frame a real problem as a scoped proposal with measurable success criteria and an agreed team charter.
Review prior work systematically and position a project against existing solutions with correct citation.
Plan a project with a work breakdown, milestones, critical path and a scored risk register.
Design and run an evaluation with sound metrics, baselines and statistics, and report limits honestly.
Deliver a versioned, tested and documented artefact through iterative sprints.
Present and defend the project in a timed demo and a question-and-answer panel.

units.title: Problem framing, scoping and teams
topics: Finding a problem worth solving: stakeholder interviews, pain points and opportunity statements
Problem statements, SMART objectives and measurable success criteria
Scoping: in and out of scope, MoSCoW prioritisation and the minimum viable deliverable
Team charters, roles, working agreements and conflict resolution
Feasibility screening: technical, economic, schedule and ethical tests
Writing the proposal: structure, one-page pitch and supervisor review

units.title: Literature and prior-art review
topics: Searching scholarly databases, patent records, open-source repositories and grey literature
Reading papers and documentation critically: claims, evidence and limits
The prior-art matrix: comparing existing solutions on features, cost and constraints
Citation practice, paraphrasing, plagiarism and referencing styles (IEEE and APA)
Gap statements and the value claim of a project

units.title: Planning, process and risk
topics: Work breakdown structures and estimation: three-point estimates and planning poker
Milestones, dependencies, Gantt charts, critical path and schedule buffers
Risk registers: likelihood, impact, mitigation and contingency
Process models for student teams: iterative, Scrum-lite and Kanban
Team tooling: Git branching, issue tracking, shared documents and a definition of done
Budget and resource planning: effort, free-tier cloud services, data and device costs

units.title: Requirements, design and experiment design
topics: Eliciting requirements: user stories, use cases and acceptance criteria
Functional and non-functional requirements; traceability matrix
Architecture sketches and architecture decision records
Design alternatives and trade-off analysis with a weighted decision matrix
Data and experiment design: datasets, sampling, baselines, hypotheses and consent
Low-fidelity prototypes and early validation with users

units.title: Implementation and iteration
topics: Sprint cycles, vertical slices and incremental delivery
Version control workflow: branches, pull requests, code review and merge conflicts
Testing strategy: unit, integration and acceptance tests
Continuous integration, environments and release with rollback
Change requests, scope control and technical debt
Debugging with logs and monitoring
Reproducibility: pinned dependencies, seeds and recorded configuration

units.title: Evaluation and results
topics: Evaluation plans: metrics, baselines and benchmarks
Usability testing: think-aloud sessions, task success and the SUS questionnaire
Performance and reliability measurement, including load tests
Statistical reporting: confidence intervals, effect sizes and threats to validity
Negative results and honest limitations
Ethics, privacy, security and social impact review

units.title: Reporting and documentation
topics: Report structure: abstract, method, results and discussion
Technical documentation: README, user guide, API notes and deployment runbook
Figures, tables and captions that carry the evidence
Individual contribution statements and fair peer assessment
Handover and maintenance plans

units.title: Presentation, demonstration and defence
topics: Structuring a talk: story arc, one message per slide and timing
Live demonstration planning: scripted demo, fallback recording and pre-flight checks
Explaining the work to a non-technical community partner
Handling questions: rehearsal with a mock panel and rubric-based assessment
Marking against a rubric and giving useful peer feedback
Release and showcase: licence choice, citation file and portfolio

schedule.title: Choosing and framing a problem
schedule.exercise: Interview a classmate about a daily frustration, turn the notes into a one-sentence problem statement with two measurable success criteria, and agree a draft team charter.

tasks.title: Interview a simulated stakeholder in the scenario engine, record five pain points with supporting evidence, and rank them by frequency and severity
Rewrite a vague client request as a problem statement with three measurable success criteria, then test each criterion against the interview evidence collected
Resolve a simulated team conflict over uneven workload by revising the charter, roles and check-in rules, and justify each change you make

schedule.title: Scope, feasibility and the proposal
schedule.exercise: Cut a brief with twelve wished-for features down to a minimum viable deliverable, screen the idea for feasibility, and draft a one-page proposal.

tasks.title: Draw a context diagram of a given project idea and mark each feature as must, should, could or won't have using MoSCoW labels
Screen four project ideas for technical, economic, schedule and ethical feasibility in a scenario and justify which idea survives each test
Write a one-page proposal for a chosen idea and revise it after two simulated reviewer comments, recording which scope cuts and risks you accepted

schedule.title: Finding and judging prior work
schedule.exercise: Find eight sources on a project topic, summarise three of them with claim, evidence and limit, and write a gap statement supported by a prior-art matrix.

tasks.title: Write a script that filters a provided CSV of 200 paper records by year, keyword and citation count, and export a shortlist of 15 with reasons
Build a prior-art matrix comparing four existing solutions on five criteria from provided summaries, and mark the cell that reveals the gap
Review a draft literature section with four citation errors, one over-close paraphrase and one unsupported claim, and correct each with a proper IEEE reference

schedule.title: Work breakdown, schedule and risk
schedule.exercise: Break a project into at least twenty tasks with estimates, draw its Gantt chart and list the ten biggest risks with mitigations.

tasks.title: Break a project brief into a work breakdown structure of at least 20 tasks with owners and three-point estimates in the diagram studio
Build a Gantt chart for a 12-week project with milestones and dependencies, find the critical path and report the total float of two tasks
Build a risk register of ten risks for a scenario project, score likelihood and impact, and choose mitigations that fit a fixed budget of effort

schedule.title: Process, tooling and budget
schedule.exercise: Choose a process model for your team and justify it, set up a repository and issue labels, and cost the cloud and data needs of the project.

tasks.title: Create a Git repository with main and feature branches, a README, an issue-labelling convention and a definition-of-done checklist for a team of four
Pick a process model for a four-person team facing changing client requirements and a hard deadline, and defend the choice in a scenario review
Plan the cloud and data budget for a student project on free tiers, set a spending alert, and find which service exceeds its free quota first

schedule.title: Requirements, design and experiment design
schedule.exercise: Write six user stories with acceptance criteria, record two architecture decisions, and design the evaluation experiment for your project hypothesis.

tasks.title: Write six user stories with acceptance criteria from stakeholder notes and check that each is independent, testable and small enough for one sprint
Draw a block architecture for a given project and record two architecture decision records stating options considered, the choice and the consequences
Design an evaluation experiment for a given hypothesis by choosing a baseline, sample size and metric, doing a power calculation and listing three threats to validity

schedule.title: Sprints, version control and testing
schedule.exercise: Plan three one-week sprints from a backlog, describe your pull-request and review rules, and write acceptance tests for the first sprint's stories.

tasks.title: Make a branch, commit two changes, open a simulated pull request and resolve a merge conflict between two team members' edits to the same file
Write unit tests for a provided function with three planted bugs, and confirm that each bug is caught by at least one failing test
Plan three one-week sprints from a backlog of 25 stories sliced vertically, and replan after a simulated mid-sprint change request

schedule.title: Delivery, change and reproducibility
schedule.exercise: Describe how your project is built, deployed and rolled back, log one real bug from report to fix, and write the steps that let a stranger reproduce your results.

tasks.title: Add structured logging to a failing program and use the log output to locate the faulty line, then write the one-line fix and a regression test
Pin dependencies, set a random seed and write a run script so that a provided experiment reproduces identical results on two clean runs
Deploy a sample web app to a cloud console with a health check, release a faulty version, and roll back to the previous version
Handle three change requests arriving late in a scenario project by weighing cost, risk and value, and decide which to accept, defer or refuse

schedule.title: Evaluation design: metrics, users and load
schedule.exercise: Choose three metrics and a baseline for your project, plan a five-person usability session, and decide what load your system must survive.

tasks.title: Run a think-aloud usability session in a scenario with five simulated users, record task success and time, and compute the SUS score
Choose three metrics and a baseline for a provided project, compute them on a supplied results table, and plot them with error bars
Run a load test against a sample service at rising request rates, find the breaking point, and recommend a fix backed by the latency graph

schedule.title: Statistics, honest limits and ethics review
schedule.exercise: Compare two versions of a system with a confidence interval, rewrite an overclaiming result honestly, and list four ethical or security risks of your own project.

tasks.title: Compute the mean, 95 percent confidence interval and effect size for two versions of a system from 30 runs each, and state whether the difference is real
Rewrite an overclaiming results section into an honest one that reports a negative result, its likely causes and what was not tested
Run an ethics, privacy and security review of a scenario project, find four risks to users or communities, and add mitigations to the design

schedule.title: Writing the report and documentation
schedule.exercise: Outline the final report with a word budget per section, write a 150-word abstract, and draft the README and handover notes for your project.

tasks.title: Write a README with install, run and test steps in a clean virtual machine, and confirm a newcomer can follow it to a running system
Create three figures from a supplied results file with labelled axes, units, captions and colour-blind-safe styling, and explain what each one shows
Write individual contribution statements and a fair peer assessment for a four-person scenario team with uneven commit history, citing evidence for each rating

schedule.title: Talks, demos and community audiences
schedule.exercise: Cut a 20-slide draft to a ten-minute talk, write a demo script with a fallback plan, and explain your project to a non-technical visitor in two minutes.

tasks.title: Cut a 20-slide draft talk to 10 minutes with one message per slide and a clear story arc, then check the timing against a simulated clock
Prepare a scripted live demo with a fallback recording and a pre-flight checklist, then recover from a simulated outage injected during the run
Present a project to a non-technical community partner in a scenario and adapt your explanation after three confused questions

schedule.title: Defence, assessment and release
schedule.exercise: Hold a mock defence with a rubric, give written peer feedback on another team's project, and publish your work with a licence and citation file.

tasks.title: Choose an open-source licence for a finished project from four options by checking dependency compatibility, then add LICENSE and citation files to the repository
Score a sample capstone report against a four-criterion rubric, justify each mark with evidence, and compare your marks with a reference panel
Defend a project before a simulated three-person panel, answering twelve questions on scope, method, evidence and limitations, and be scored on a rubric
